title: Cellular Respiration Overview
content: The mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell, responsible for producing ATP through cellular respiration. This process involves the electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation. The citric acid cycle, also known as the Krebs cycle, occurs in the mitochondrial matrix and produces electron carriers that drive ATP synthesis.

title: Photosynthesis in Plants
content: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, converting light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose molecules. The process involves two stages: the light-dependent reactions in the thylakoid membranes and the Calvin cycle in the stroma. Chlorophyll absorbs primarily blue and red light wavelengths.

title: The French Revolution
content: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille. It led to the end of the monarchy and the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte. The revolution was driven by social inequality, financial crisis, and Enlightenment ideals. The Reign of Terror saw thousands executed by guillotine.

title: The Renaissance Period
content: The Renaissance was a cultural movement that began in Italy in the 14th century, spreading throughout Europe over the next few centuries. It marked a renewed interest in classical Greek and Roman culture. Key figures included Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Raphael.

title: Amazon Rainforest Ecosystem
content: The Amazon rainforest produces approximately 20% of the world's oxygen. Deforestation threatens this vital ecosystem. The rainforest spans nine countries and contains 10% of all species on Earth. Indigenous communities have lived sustainably in the Amazon for thousands of years.

title: Coral Reef Biodiversity
content: Coral reefs support 25% of all marine species despite covering less than 1% of the ocean floor. Rising ocean temperatures cause coral bleaching, threatening these ecosystems. The Great Barrier Reef has lost over half its coral since 1995.

title: Python Programming Language
content: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It emphasizes code readability with its use of significant indentation. Python supports multiple programming paradigms including procedural, object-oriented, and functional programming. It has become the most popular language for data science and machine learning.

title: JavaScript for Web Development
content: JavaScript is the most popular programming language for web development, running in browsers and on servers via Node.js. It was created by Brendan Eich in 1995. Modern JavaScript includes features like async/await, modules, and arrow functions.

title: Type 1 Diabetes Overview
content: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition where the pancreas produces little or no insulin. It typically develops in childhood or adolescence. Patients require lifelong insulin therapy. The exact cause is unknown but involves genetic and environmental factors.

title: Gestational Diabetes
content: Gestational diabetes occurs during pregnancy and usually resolves after delivery, though it increases risk of type 2 diabetes later. It affects about 6-9% of pregnancies. Management includes diet modification, exercise, and sometimes insulin.

title: Angular Framework Overview
content: Angular is a TypeScript-based framework developed by Google. It uses a component-based architecture similar to React. Angular includes built-in tools for routing, forms, and HTTP communication. It follows a more opinionated structure than other frameworks.

title: Vue.js Introduction
content: Vue.js offers a progressive framework that can be adopted incrementally. It's known for its gentle learning curve. Vue combines the best features of React and Angular while maintaining simplicity. The framework was created by Evan You in 2014.

title: Kyoto Cultural Heritage

title: 2008 Financial Crisis Response
content: The 2008 crisis led to significant regulatory changes including the Dodd-Frank Act, which imposed stricter oversight on financial institutions. The act created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and established new rules for derivatives trading.

title: TARP Bailout Program

title: 2008 Crisis Employment Impact
content: Unemployment peaked at 10% in October 2009 as the effects of the crisis rippled through the economy. Over 8.7 million jobs were lost between 2008 and 2010. The recovery took years, with employment not returning to pre-crisis levels until 2014.

title: Aspirin Uses and Dosage
content: Aspirin is commonly used to reduce fever, relieve mild to moderate pain, and reduce inflammation. It's also used as a blood thinner to prevent heart attacks and strokes. The recommended dosage for adults is typically 325-650mg every 4-6 hours as needed, not exceeding 4g per day.

title: Aspirin Side Effects
content: Side effects of aspirin may include stomach upset, heartburn, and in rare cases, gastrointestinal bleeding. Long-term use can increase bleeding risk. Aspirin should not be given to children with viral infections due to risk of Reye's syndrome.

title: Ming Dynasty Great Wall Construction
content: The Great Wall was primarily built during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), with most existing sections dating to this period. The Ming wall stretches over 5,500 miles. Construction employed millions of workers over centuries.

title: Qin Dynasty Wall Origins
content: Construction of the Great Wall began during the Qin Dynasty under Emperor Qin Shi Huang around 221 BC. The emperor connected existing fortifications into a unified defense system. Much of the original Qin wall has eroded.

title: Ancient Chinese Fortifications
content: Archaeological evidence suggests wall-building in China dates back to the 7th century BC, predating unified China. Various states built walls for defense against nomadic tribes. These early walls were primarily earthen structures.

title: Asteroid Impact Theory
content: The asteroid impact theory, supported by the Chicxulub crater, is now the scientific consensus for dinosaur extinction. The impact released energy equivalent to billions of nuclear bombs. The resulting impact winter blocked sunlight for years.

title: Deccan Traps Volcanic Theory
content: Volcanic activity from the Deccan Traps in India released massive amounts of gases, causing climate change that killed the dinosaurs. The eruptions lasted for about 800,000 years. Sulfur dioxide and carbon dioxide altered global temperatures.

title: Combined Extinction Theory
content: Some scientists argue it was a combination of asteroid impact and volcanic activity that led to the mass extinction. The asteroid may have triggered increased volcanic activity. Both factors contributed to rapid climate change.

title: British Inquiry Titanic Report
content: The official British inquiry concluded that 1,503 people died when the Titanic sank on April 15, 1912. The inquiry found the ship was traveling too fast in an ice field. Captain Smith was posthumously criticized for his decisions.

title: US Senate Titanic Investigation
content: The US Senate investigation put the death toll at 1,517, based on different passenger manifest interpretations. The investigation led to new maritime safety regulations. It established requirements for sufficient lifeboats.

title: Modern Titanic Death Toll Analysis
content: Recent historical analysis suggests the actual number may be closer to 1,496, accounting for name duplications in records. Some passengers used aliases. The exact count remains debated among historians.

title: Stanford Remote Work Study
content: A Stanford study found remote workers were 13% more productive, with fewer breaks and sick days. The study tracked call center employees over two years. Workers reported higher job satisfaction and lower attrition.

title: Harvard Remote Work Analysis
content: A Harvard study found productivity varied significantly by role - creative work suffered while routine tasks improved. Knowledge workers showed mixed results. The research suggests hybrid models may be optimal.

title: Remote Work Measurement Challenges

title: Coffee and Cardiovascular Health

title: Coffee Side Effects and Risks

title: Genetics and Coffee Metabolism

title: Coffee During Pregnancy
